paper.title: Federated Online and Bandit Convex Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Federated online convex optimization with first-order feedback, adversary class P(F^G, zeta)
unmapped: feedback is a single gradient of f_t^m at the queried point (first-order oracle), not full information
M machines with intermittent communication: R communication rounds, K steps between them, T = KR
comparator is shared across machines and lies in the L2 ball of radius B; plays unconstrained in R^d
bounded first-order heterogeneity zeta across machines (Assumption 1)
adversary adaptive to past models but not to the machines' random seeds
settings.definition_quote: We consider the following distributed regret minimization problem on $M$ machines over a horizon of length $T$: \sum_{m\in[M], t\in [T]}f_t^m(x_t^m) - \min_{\norm{x^\star}\leq B} \sum_{m\in[M], t\in [T]}f_t^m(x^\star)

settings.name_in_paper: Federated online convex optimization with first-order feedback, adversary class P(F^H, zeta) (smooth)
unmapped: first-order (gradient) feedback at queried point
M machines, intermittent communication T = KR
comparator in L2 ball radius B
F_star: average value of the losses at the optimum (non-negative smooth functions)
settings.definition_quote: $\boldsymbol{\fff^{H}}$, the class of convex, differentiable, and $H$-smooth functions

settings.name_in_paper: Federated adversarial linear bandits, one-point bandit feedback, P(F_lin^G, zeta)
unmapped: M machines, R communication rounds, K local steps, T = KR
loss vectors beta_t^m in L2 ball of radius G; comparator in L2 ball radius B
bounded first-order heterogeneity zeta; learner tunes step size using B, M, K, zeta
settings.definition_quote: at each time $t\in[T]$, an agent $m\in[M]$ chooses an action $x_t^m\in\rr^d$ while simultaneously environment picks $\beta_t^m\in \bb_2(G)\subset \rr^d$. Agent $m$ then suffers the loss $f_t^m(x_t^m)=\langle\beta_t^m,x_t^m\rangle$.

settings.name_in_paper: Federated bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback, P(F^G, zeta)
unmapped: M machines, intermittent communication T = KR
regret incurred at both queried points
comparator in L2 ball radius B
bounded heterogeneity zeta
settings.definition_quote: Function values of $f_t^m$ at two different points, a.k.a., two-point bandit feedback.

settings.name_in_paper: Federated bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback, P(F^{G,H}, zeta)
unmapped: M machines, intermittent communication T = KR
comparator in L2 ball radius B
bounded heterogeneity zeta
F_star average value at optimum
settings.definition_quote: We also define $\boldsymbol{\fff^{G, H}} := \boldsymbol{\fff^{G}}\cap \boldsymbol{\fff^{H}}$, i.e., the class of Lipschitz and smooth functions.

settings.name_in_paper: Federated adversarial linear bandits with two-point feedback, P(F_lin^G, zeta)
unmapped: M machines, intermittent communication T = KR
comparator in L2 ball radius B
bounded heterogeneity zeta
settings.definition_quote: $\boldsymbol{\fff_{lin}^{G}} \subset \boldsymbol{\fff^{G, H}}$, which includes linear cost functions with gradients bounded by $G$.

symbols.B_comp: norm bound B on the comparator

tuning: eta tuned as in classical OGD (order B/(G sqrt(T)))

source.label: thm:first_lip
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg:NC_OGD} incurs an average regret of $\ooo\rb{GB/\sqrt{T}}$ against the adversary class $\ppp(\fff^{G}, \zeta)$, where $B$ is the norm of the comparator. This regret is optimal ... i.e., $\rrr(\ppp(\fff^{G}, \zeta), \aaa_{IC}^1) = \Theta(GB/\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Paper bounds average regret over M machines and T rounds; multiplied by M*T to get total regret summed over machines. Paper's G is L_lip.

symbols.B_comp: norm bound B on the comparator

conditions: hard instance uses linear losses identical across machines (stochastic, coordinated)
algorithms in A_IC^1 (intermittent communication, first-order oracle)

source.label: thm:first_lip
source.quote: This regret is optimal against adversaries from $\ppp(\fff^{G, B}, \zeta)$ among algorithms in $\aaa_{IC}^1$, where $0\leq\zeta\leq 2G$, i.e., $\rrr(\ppp(\fff^{G}, \zeta), \aaa_{IC}^1) = \Theta(GB/\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Average regret lower bound GB/(2 sqrt T) from proof; multiplied by M*T. Also characterizes the linear class since instance is linear.

symbols.F_star: average loss value at the optimum (Definition 2.2)

tuning: OGD step size as in Srebro et al. 2010

source.label: thm:first_smth
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg:NC_OGD} incurs the optimal regret of $\Theta\rb{HB^2/T + \sqrt{HF_\star}B/\sqrt{T}}$ against adversary class $\ppp(\fff^{H}, \zeta)$, where $B$ is the norm of the comparator and $F_\star$ is from definition \ref{ass:loss_optimal}.

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by M*T. H is smoothness (beta). Upper bound follows from serial OGD optimistic rates.

symbols.F_star: average loss value at the optimum

conditions: coordinated (identical across machines) stochastic hard instance from Woodworth & Srebro 2021

source.label: thm:first_smth
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg:NC_OGD} incurs the optimal regret of $\Theta\rb{HB^2/T + \sqrt{HF_\star}B/\sqrt{T}}$ against adversary class $\ppp(\fff^{H}, \zeta)$

results.notes: Lower bound part of Theta claim; average regret multiplied by M*T.

symbols.K_gap: number of local steps between communications (paper's K)
symbols.R_comm: number of communication rounds R; T = K_gap*R_comm

conditions: loss vectors in L2 ball of radius G
tuning: eta = B/(G sqrt(T)) * min{1, sqrt(M)/(dB), 1/(sqrt(dB) K^{1/4}), sqrt(G)/sqrt(zeta K)}

source.label: thm:favlb
source.quote: Against the adversary class $\ppp(\fff_{lin}^{G},\zeta)$, if we choose $\eta = ...$ and $\delta=B$, the queried points ... satisfy: \frac{1}{MKR}\sum ... \preceq \frac{GB}{\sqrt{KR}} + \frac{GB d}{\sqrt{MKR}} + \mathbbm{1}_{K>1}\cdot\rb{\frac{GB\sqrt{d}}{K^{1/4}\sqrt{R}}+\frac{\sqrt{G\zeta}B}{\sqrt{R}}}

results.notes: Average regret over M machines and KR rounds multiplied by M*K*R. Regret through expectation over algorithm randomness against fixed comparator for linear losses; classified pseudo_regret/expected ambiguous since adversary deterministic. For K=1 the indicator terms vanish (separate result).

symbols.R_comm: number of communication rounds (= T when K=1)

results.notes: K=1 branch of Theorem 5.1; average regret multiplied by M*T.

tuning: eta = B/(G sqrt(T)) * min{1, sqrt(M)/sqrt(d), 1/(sqrt(K) d^{1/4})}

source.label: thm:bd_grad_first_stoch
source.quote: Against the adversary class class $\ppp(\fff^{G}, \zeta)$, if we choose $\eta = ...$, and $\delta = ...$, the queried points ... of Algorithm \ref{alg:fed_ogd} satisfy: \frac{1}{2MKR}\sum ... \preceq \frac{GB}{\sqrt{KR}} + \frac{GB\sqrt{d}}{\sqrt{MKR}} + \mathbbm{1}_{K>1}\cdot\frac{GBd^{1/4}}{\sqrt{R}}

results.notes: Average regret over 2MKR queries; multiplied by M*K*R (regret per query point averaged over the two). Regret counted at both queried points.
K=1 branch; paper says this is tight (matches Appendix A lower bound).

tuning: eta and delta as in Lemma D.1 (appendix)

source.label: thm:smooth_first_stoch
source.quote: Against the adversary class $\ppp(\fff^{G,H}, \zeta)$. If we choose appropriate $\eta, \delta$ ..., the queried points ... of Algorithm \ref{alg:fed_ogd} satisfy: ... \preceq \frac{HB^2}{KR} + \frac{\sqrt{HF_\star}B}{\sqrt{KR}} + \frac{GB}{\sqrt{KR}}+ \frac{ GB\sqrt{d}}{\sqrt{MKR}} +\mathbbm{1}_{K>1}\cdot\min\{...\}

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by M*K*R. Theorem also states the Theorem 6.1 bound is attainable with the corresponding step size. Note the statement includes both GB/sqrt(KR) and sqrt(HF*)B/sqrt(KR) terms (the lemma has a min of them).

tuning: same eta and delta as Theorem 6.2 with H = 0

source.label: coro:linear
source.quote: Against the adversary class $\ppp(\fff^{G}_{lin}, \zeta)$, if we choose the same $\eta$ and $\delta$ as in Theorem \ref{thm:smooth_first_stoch} (with $H=0$), the queried points ... satisfy: ... \preceq \frac{GB}{\sqrt{KR}} + \frac{ GB\sqrt{d}}{\sqrt{MKR}} + \mathbbm{1}_{K>1}\cdot \rb{\frac{\sqrt{\zeta G}Bd^{1/4}}{K^{1/4}\sqrt{R}} + \frac{\zeta B}{\sqrt{R}}}

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by M*K*R. For K=1 or zeta=0 reduces to the first two terms (optimal).

tuning: same eta and delta as Theorem 6.2 with H = 0

conditions: algorithms in A_IC^{0,2} (two-point bandit feedback, intermittent communication)

source.label: sec:lower_bounds
source.quote: We want to prove a lower bound for the adversary class $\ppp(\fff^{G})$ with two-point bandit feedback. In particular, we want to show that \rrr(\ppp(\fff^{G}, \zeta), \aaa^{0,2}_{IC}) \succeq \frac{GB}{\sqrt{KR}} + \frac{GB\sqrt{d}}{\sqrt{MKR}}.

results.notes: Not in a theorem environment; proof sketch via Duchi et al. 2015 Proposition 2. Average regret multiplied by M*K*R.
